content: Spec writing: 2-lead structure with research lead + spec-writer lead. Research lead sends findings via mail, writer lead spawns builder for draft then reviser to integrate research. Avoids file conflicts, enables iteration.

M0 scaffolding: single lead with single builder is sufficient. M1 implementation: split into 2 parallel leads by file area (scanner vs graph/cache/CLI). Non-overlapping file scopes prevent merge conflicts. Graph lead merged first, parsing lead took longer due to tree-sitter complexity + 2 stalled builders before successful 3rd attempt.

M2 decomposition: 2 leads (WASM/layout vs web/server). WASM lead finished first (simpler Rust-only). Web lead split into rust-server-builder + web-ui-builder (3 attempts needed for JS/TS builder — complex npm/bundling tasks stall builders frequently). Merge order matters when builders share files: merge server first, then UI (UI has definitive main.ts).
